How these numbers were put together

Sales come from 16 Maui County parcel snapshots taken between January 2025 and November 2026, so sales later overwritten by a $1 deed or a resale are still counted. Each row is one parcel.

A lot without a house means the county roll valued the home at $0 after the fire, the lot was vacant before the fire, or the lot was newly created. Houses are homes the county still valued after the fire, plus one new home LCLT bought.

Lahaina means a mailing address in Lahaina, Napili, Kaanapali, Kapalua, Kahana, Honokowai or Olowalu, plus LCLT. Addresses are all from after the fire, so a displaced Lahaina family now mailing from Kahului or Oahu counts as outside Lahaina unless a deed or other record shows they lived in Lahaina before the fire. Out-of-state means a mainland or foreign address. An LLC counts wherever it mails from.

Seller addresses come from the snapshot before each sale and from LCLT’s own deed research. Missing seller and buyer addresses were filled from Hawaii Bureau of Conveyances deeds. A few transfers that weren’t sales still lack an address and show as unknown.

Prepared by Unwind Housing on behalf of Lahaina Community Land Trust in collaboration with Claude, from Maui County parcel records. Data as of November 11, 2026; page built 2026-11-11. No owner, buyer or seller names are included.
